title: Data-Driven Evaluation of Cryo-EM Micrographs Using Self-Supervised Learning
content: Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a leading technique for resolving high-resolution, three-dimensional biomolecular structures [1-3]. The success of 3D reconstruction is highly dependent on the size and quality of datasets, as millions of particle images must be averaged to overcome the problem of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). With advancements in automation and high-throughput data acquisition, a single imaging session can generate tens of thousands of micrographs [4, 5]. However, new challenges arise when identifying high-quality micrographs among those collected. To achieve accurate structures, micrographs must contain high-resolution exposures from randomly oriented molecules embedded in thin, vitreous ice; while excluding unwanted grid areas containing contaminants, support film, cracks, and crystalline ice [6-8].
